notes: 20-item bank. CAPS mix: 10 L2 / 10 L3. Topics: recognise inverse from tables/graphs/scenarios; product = constant; shared-cost contexts.

stimulus.inline: Inverse proportion: as x grows, y shrinks, and x × y stays the same constant.

items.question:
Which table shows an INVERSE proportion?

**Table A:**
| x | y |
|---|---|
| 1 | 24 |
| 2 | 12 |
| 3 | 8 |
| 4 | 6 |

**Table B:**
| x | y |
|---|---|
| 1 | 5 |
| 2 | 10 |
| 3 | 15 |
| 4 | 20 |
workingSteps: Table B: y rises with x — direct, not inverse.

stimulus.inline:
A taxi-scheme costs R6 000/month fixed. Teachers share equally.

| Teachers | Cost each (R) |
|---|---|
| 5 | 1 200 |
| 10 | 600 |
| 12 | 500 |
| 20 | 300 |

items.question: Confirm: as the number of teachers increases, what happens to the cost each?
workingSteps: Each row: teachers × cost = R6 000 (constant). Inverse proportion.

stimulus.inline: An inverse-proportion graph is a CURVE (not a straight line) that drops sharply for small x and flattens out for large x.

items.question: Which scenario has an inverse-proportion graph?
options: Speed × time to cover a fixed 240 km trip.
Wage at R85/hour vs hours worked.
items.expectedAnswer: Speed × time to cover a fixed 240 km trip.
workingSteps: For a fixed distance, speed × time = 240 (constant). Faster speed = less time. Inverse.

stimulus.inline:

- Plan Y: monthly fee R200, no per-min charge.

items.question: Which plan has an INVERSE relationship between minutes used and effective cost-per-minute?
workingSteps: Plan Y: total cost = R200 (constant). Cost-per-minute = R200 ÷ minutes — falls as minutes rise.
Plan X: per-minute cost is fixed at R0,80 (not inverse).

items.question: What kind of curve does an inverse-proportion graph make?
options: A straight line through the origin.
A descending curve that flattens out (hyperbola shape).
items.expectedAnswer: A descending curve that flattens out (hyperbola shape).
workingSteps: Inverse-proportion graphs have a hyperbola shape — drops fast, then levels.

_error_signal_vocabulary.ERR_INVERSE_AS_DIRECT: Treats an inverse scenario as direct (more = more, instead of more = less).
_error_signal_vocabulary.ERR_INVERSE_PRODUCT_CONSTANT: Does not recognise that x × y is the constant in an inverse relationship.
_error_signal_vocabulary.ERR_INVERSE_OPERATION: Uses the wrong operation after finding the constant product.
_error_signal_vocabulary.ERR_FIXED_COST_SPLIT_DIRECTION: Splits a fixed cost in the wrong direction.
_error_signal_vocabulary.ERR_RELATIONSHIP_TYPE: Misclassifies the type of relationship (constant, linear, inverse, compound).
_error_signal_vocabulary.ERR_SPEED_TIME_DISTANCE: Confuses the inverse speed × time = distance relationship for a fixed distance.
_error_signal_vocabulary.ERR_RATE_USE_OPERATION: Uses the wrong operation when applying a known rate.
_error_signal_vocabulary.ERR_GRAPH_SHAPE_READ: Misinterprets the shape of an inverse-proportion graph (e.g. thinks it's a straight line).
